solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Measure of wire, almost 1,760 yards (3)

indicators.note: almost the whole word: the last letter is left off

blocks.note: 1,760 yards is a MILE; almost all of it drops the final E

explanation.surface: Someone is measuring off nearly a mile of wire.
explanation.walkthrough: The number reads as a length of wire to be cut, but 1,760 yards is simply a mile, written in figures to hide the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mil is a thousandth of an inch, the unit used for the thickness of wire.

clue.text: Hog swimming in some pool (10)

indicators.note: letters swimming about are moved out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A pig is swimming in a pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hog' looks like the animal; it is the verb, to keep something for yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To hog something is to monopolise it, keeping it all to yourself.

clue.text: Bound to put small donation in hat (7)

indicators.note: the donation is put somewhere
in means inside, so the small donation sits inside the hat

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat; it holds the next piece
a mite is a tiny sum, from the Bible's widow's mite

explanation.surface: Someone is bound to drop a small coin into a collecting hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but 'Bound' alone is the definition and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound is limited, confined within limits.

clue.text: Doing without us is of necessity (11)

indicators.note: in its old sense of 'outside': PERFORCE sits outside MAN

blocks.note: perforce means of necessity; it is split around the next piece
us, humankind, is man

explanation.surface: Something we cannot manage without is said to be essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, so the letters for 'of necessity' wrap around MAN, which is 'us' in the sense of the human race.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is a doing, as when a play or task is performed.

clue.text: Fictional lawyer is held up – and down, perhaps (9,6)

indicators.note: the letters might perhaps be arranged another way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: A lawyer in a novel is kept waiting, and may be depressed too.
explanation.walkthrough: Pudd'nhead Wilson is Mark Twain's small-town lawyer who solves a murder with fingerprints. 'Up and down' reads as a mood; it is all fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: David 'Pudd'nhead' Wilson is the lawyer hero of Mark Twain's 1894 novel.

clue.text: Could remember being withdrawn (8)

blocks.note: the past tense of bringing something back to mind
as a faulty product or an ambassador is called back

explanation.surface: Someone shy remembered a quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' suggests a shy person; it means called back.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalled means both remembered and called back, withdrawn.

clue.text: Twist, say, for rising Chinese dynasty (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, so PRO goes backwards

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour
the Han dynasty ruled China from 206 BC

explanation.surface: Someone backs a rising Chinese dynasty, with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like a turn or a dance; with 'say' it is Oliver Twist, Dickens's orphan boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is literature's best-known orphan, so he is one example of an orphan.

clue.text: Part of railway signal hardly bent after damage (11,4)

indicators.note: the letters are bent out of shape
the rearranged letters come after MAR

blocks.note: to mar is to damage
anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.surface: A railway signal is barely bent after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface stays on the railway throughout, which makes 'signal' hard to see as mere fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshalling yard is the part of a railway where wagons are sorted into trains.

clue.text: Country — one with capital in Abuja (7)

definitions.text: Country — one with capital in Abuja

indicators.note: the capital letter of Abuja is its first, A

blocks.note: the West African state of NIGER, on the river of the same name
I is the Roman numeral one
the capital (first) letter of Abuja

explanation.surface: A plain description of a country whose capital is Abuja.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines Nigeria, whose capital really is Abuja, while the words also build it: one country, then I, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue is a plain fact: Abuja has been the capital since 1991, replacing Lagos.

clue.text: Bird in another nest (4)

indicators.note: the bird sits in the letters that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of 'another' and the first two of 'nest'

explanation.surface: A bird has moved into a different nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The erne sits across the two words, like a cuckoo in another bird's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle.

clue.text: Homeless alternative comedian leaving Spain (7)

indicators.note: an alternative version of the word is a rearrangement of its letters
the E for Spain leaves the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder before the deletion
E is Spain's international vehicle code (España); it is removed, leaving COMDIAN to rearrange

explanation.surface: An alternative comic has left Spain and now has nowhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative comedian' reads as a style of stand-up, but 'alternative' is the rearranging instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people have no fixed home, moving from place to place.

clue.text: Pop music playing, which is ideal (7)

blocks.note: pop and pa are both words for father
a rag is a piece of ragtime music
a show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: Someone declares that having pop music on is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop music' is one idea in the surface, but it splits into dad and a ragtime tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Here ideal is the noun, the perfect example to copy, which is a close synonym.

clue.text: When finished, hide plain belt (6,7)

blocks.note: patent means obvious, plain to see
to leather someone is to belt them, to thrash them

explanation.surface: An instruction to hide a plain belt once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb and 'belt' like a noun; in fact hide is animal skin and belt is a verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent leather is hide given a hard glossy finish.

clue.text: Trying to hide the evidence of aging? (10)

indicators.note: WEARING hides THE inside it

blocks.note: trying, as in tiring, is wearing; it holds the next piece
as written

explanation.surface: Someone is covering up the signs of getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying to hide' reads as an attempt at concealment; 'Trying' is WEARING and 'to hide' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Weathering is the wear left on stone, wood or skin by age and exposure.

clue.text: Having run, boy runs into activity (8)

indicators.note: runs go into the activity, so its letters are placed inside

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
a deed is an act; it takes in the R
R = runs, as in cricket scores

explanation.surface: A boy, fresh from a run, throws himself into some activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having run' sounds like a jogger, but it is said of tights or stockings with a ladder in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddered tights have a run, a vertical line of broken stitches.

clue.text: Magic word appeals to audience (6)

indicators.note: an audience hears the word, so the answer is how it sounds

blocks.note: pleas are appeals; said, the word is identical

explanation.surface: A magician's special word wins over the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The magic word is the one children are taught to say when asking for something, not a spell like abracadabra.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Please' is the magic word parents tell children to use when they ask for something.

clue.text: Brilliant boy progresses quickly (6,2)

blocks.note: a crack shot is a brilliant one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A gifted child is racing ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: To crack on is British informal for getting on with something briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cracks on presses ahead fast with a task.

clue.text: Drink with timid guards (6)

indicators.note: SHY guards, surrounds, AND

blocks.note: timid means shy; it goes around the next piece
with = and, as in 'fish with chips'

explanation.surface: A nervous guard is having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joining word, but it supplies AND, which the letters for 'timid' hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a drink of beer mixed with lemonade, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Declare source of heat arising in volcanic lake (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means reading upward, so SUN goes backwards

blocks.note: to aver is to declare
the sun is our source of heat

explanation.surface: Someone announces that heat is welling up in a crater lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Avernus is a crater lake near Naples which the Romans took for the entrance to the underworld, so heat rising there suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Avernus fills an extinct volcanic crater in southern Italy.

clue.text: Coach went down minor diversion (5,3)

blocks.note: to coach is to train
the sun set, it went down

explanation.surface: A coach took a small detour.
explanation.walkthrough: The coach and the diversion suggest a bus rerouted; the diversion is a toy, a pastime for the young.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a toy railway, an amusement for minors.

clue.text: Neuter animal at home for a bit (7)

blocks.note: the snip is slang for a vasectomy, so to neuter
an animal kept at home is a pet

explanation.surface: A vet neuters an animal at home, just for a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a bit' sounds like 'for a while'; 'a bit' alone is the answer, a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small piece cut off, like a snippet of conversation.

clue.text: Fuel’s particular job, releasing energy (6)

indicators.note: to release is to let go, so the job lets go of its energy letter

blocks.note: a pet subject is a particular favourite
a role is a job, a function
E = energy, dropped from ROLE

explanation.surface: A fuel has a specific job to do: releasing energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuel releasing energy is exactly what fuel does, so the surface hides the deletion instruction in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is the British word for gasoline, a fuel.

clue.text: Father Joseph’s awfully nice men say “Revolt” (8,5)

indicators.note: done awfully, the letters are in a mess

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
e.g., for example, as 'say' does
to revolt is to rise up

explanation.surface: A priest reports that some pleasant men are calling for rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Joseph was the Capuchin friar who advised Cardinal Richelieu; the grey habit behind the red cardinal gave the phrase its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Joseph was the original éminence grise, the power behind Richelieu.

clue.text: Made cow get hitched under one? (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, WED sits under A

blocks.note: a = one, as in 'a pound'
to get hitched is to wed

explanation.surface: A cow is being married off under someone's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' reads as the animal; it is the verb, to intimidate, so 'made cow' is overawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Awed means made to cow, filled with fearful respect.

clue.text: Twists or produces a knot (7)

blocks.note: a road that twists winds
as written

explanation.surface: Twisting something ties a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a literal description of tying a tie, which is where the answer lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windsor is a wide, symmetrical knot for a necktie.

clue.text: Dog that is sent back after biting (4,3)

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so its letters run in reverse
the reversed IE comes after SHARP

blocks.note: a biting wind is sharp
i.e., id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A dog is sent away after biting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog and its bite belong together in the surface, but 'biting' is an adjective, sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: The shar pei is a Chinese breed of dog with a deeply wrinkled coat.

clue.text: Hell-bent? The opposite (11)

definitions.note: the opposite of hell-bent, i.e. unwilling; 'the opposite' stands for an adjective

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
bent means inclined, leaning

explanation.surface: Asked if they are hell-bent on something, a person says the reverse is true.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken piece by piece, hell-bent is DIS plus INCLINED; the finished word means the opposite of hell-bent, reluctant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent is determined to act; disinclined is unwilling, its opposite.

clue.text: Water tower empty when turned over (3)

indicators.note: a word turned over is flipped end to end, so its letters read backwards

blocks.note: to gut a fish or a building is to empty it

explanation.surface: A water tower is drained and knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water tower' suggests a tall tank; read it as one who tows on water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a boat that tows larger ships on the water.
